# Short answer: nothing is expired, and nothing expires in the next 30 days. But one intent is dead, and one is at real risk of silently failing.

## Dead
**`0xe88b…df16` — "Marketing tools trial - Q3"** — **Revoked** on 2026-09-13 ("Trial ended, tool not adopted"). It can't pay anything again. **0.80 USDC of your funding is still sitting in it** — withdraw the remainder.

## Expiry timeline
All four intents end at **`endTime` 1791878965–1791879029**, i.e. **~13 Oct 2026** — roughly 30 days out. No 7- or 14-day cliff to worry about right now. Worth noting they all share the same ~30-day horizon, which looks like a default rather than a deliberate per-intent choice; if you want the infra autopay to outlive the research subscriptions, that's a decision you haven't actually made yet.

## The more likely cause of an agent "stopping" before any expiry
**`0x4e08…bcf4` — "Cloud infra autopay"** is the one to watch. Both payments landed at **0.49 USDC against a 0.50 per-tx cap (98%)**, and it's already burned **49% of its 2 USDC total cap in one day**. Two separate failure modes ahead of the October expiry:
- A weekly invoice above 0.50 USDC will be **rejected by the per-tx cap**.
- At the current burn rate the **2 USDC total cap runs out well before 13 Oct** — and only 0.22 USDC of funding is left in it.

That's the one that will lapse first, and it won't be because of a date.

## Live but fine on expiry
- `0xb530…7ca7` — Research subscriptions. Active, 0.2% of a 50 USDC cap used. Separately: 50 USDC is 75% of your total authorised value for 0.10 USDC of actual spend — oversized, worth trimming.
- `0x5682…2f5b` — General ops. Active, **0 payments ever**, but **no merchant allowlist** on a 10 USDC cap. Not an expiry risk; it's an exposure one. If you can't name a counterparty for it, it has no purpose and should be revoked and drained.

**Do now:** withdraw the 0.80 USDC from the revoked marketing intent; raise the per-tx cap and top up the cloud infra autopay before the next weekly invoice.

One caveat on the data: the analysis endpoint returns expiry only as a relative `endsInDays`, so I read the absolute dates off the raw `endTime` fields in the intent list — those agree at ~13 Oct, but confirm on-chain before you act on tight timing. The withdrawable balance on the revoked intent is also worth re-checking on-chain, as no funding tx hash was exposed.

findings.title: One revoked intent holding all of the system's idle capital
findings.detail: 0xe88b02abd36a10617386cd71105ff39276ccdf16 ('Marketing tools trial - Q3') is in state Revoked with reason 'Trial ended, tool not adopted'. findings.title: Zero expired intents and no near-term expiries in this window
findings.detail: All four indexed intents report endsInDays=30 relative to generatedAt 2026-09-13T08:41:21Z, implying an expiry around 2026-10-13 for each. No intent is in state Expired, and none falls inside a typical 7- or 14-day expiry watch. The uniform 30-day value across four intents with different purposes and funding profiles looks like a shared default rather than independently set horizons.
evidence: no intent has state='Expired'; activeIntents=3 of intentCount=4

findings.title: Unrestricted, unused 10 USDC intent is the largest containment risk among live intents
findings.detail: 0x568222982112b7bd55bd90524e1434472f422f5b ('General ops agent - discretionary spend') has totalCap 10 USDC, perTxCap 2 USDC, an empty merchant allowlist (unrestrictedMerchants=true), 0 payments and 0 USDC spent, yet is funded 0.30 USDC. It carries the second-largest cap in the set with no demonstrated need and no merchant containment — it can pay anyone, up to whatever is funded, for the next ~30 days.

findings.title: Cloud infra autopay is being throttled at its per-tx cap
findings.detail: 0x4e0866d3c7ac1acbd4058cc9a0877193e640bcf4 has made both of its payments at 0.49 USDC against a 0.50 USDC perTxCap — 98% of cap on each — to the same merchant 0x1111…1111. It has consumed 49% of its 2 USDC total cap in a single day and holds only 0.22 USDC unspent funding. If real weekly GPU/storage invoices exceed 0.50 USDC, payments will fail or be split; this is a sizing problem, not an overspend problem.

actions.rationale: Intent is already Revoked and the trial tool was not adopted; 0.80 USDC of funded balance sits idle with no future payment path. This is the only recoverable capital in the set.

A 10 USDC cap with an empty allowlist and zero payments in 90 days gives the agent unbounded merchant reach for no demonstrated benefit. Pin an allowlist before any spend occurs; if no counterparty can be named, the intent has no justified purpose and should be revoked and drained instead.

Research subscriptions intent authorises 50 USDC — the largest cap in the set, 75% of all authorised value — against 0.10 USDC of observed spend (capUsedPct=0.2) and a single merchant. Cut the cap toward observed need to shrink blast radius before the ~2026-10-13 expiry.

Both payments landed at 98% of the 0.50 USDC perTxCap, indicating the agent is clipping invoices against the ceiling rather than paying true amounts. Re-size perTxCap to the actual weekly GPU/storage invoice once confirmed, or accept failed payments as infra bills arrive.

dataGaps: The feed exposes only endsInDays (relative), not absolute expiry timestamps or block heights — the ~2026-10-13 expiry dates in this review are derived from generatedAt + 30 days and should be confirmed against on-chain intent metadata.
All four intents report an identical endsInDays=30; it cannot be determined from this data whether these are genuine per-intent expiries or a protocol/indexer default.
No Expired-state intents appear in the 90-day window, so it is unknown how expired intents are represented or whether withdrawRemainder has already been called on any prior intent.
Merchant addresses (0x1111…, 0x2222…, 0x3333…) have no names or categories, so merchant-restriction advice cannot be validated against intended counterparties.
No funding or revocation transaction hashes are provided for 0xe88b…df16, so the exact withdrawable balance should be re-checked on-chain before calling withdrawRemainder.
